result.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
result.summary: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning strategies, and guide training-data refinement. Motivated by our data construction for world-model pretraining, we introduce PhysCapBench, to our knowledge the first unified physical-caption benchmark spanning all three domains: third-person scenes, egocentric manipulation, and handheld-gripper demonstrations. It provides human-verified annotations for 1,500 video sequences and evaluates accuracy and coverage through seven physical dimensions. We examine downstream utility through video reconstruction and manipulation-policy fine-tuning. Physical captions reduce reconstruction LPIPS by 8.6-9.5% on third-person videos and 26.9-30.9% on egocentric videos relative to metadata captions. Training-instruction enrichment improves both PhysCapBench scores and policy success, including a 7.5-percentage-point gain for pi0.5 on a RoboTwin 2.0 subtask. PhysCapBench makes the physical content of language supervision inspectable and comparable, providing a cross-domain basis for its evaluation and improvement.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PhysCapBench，覆盖第三人称场景、自我中心操作与手持夹爪示范三类视频共 1,500 段，用七个物理维度评价字幕的准确性与覆盖度，并以视频重建和操作策略微调检验其下游价值。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「物理维度覆盖度」这一可检查的标注质量尺度，可能可供核查语言监督是否保留交互与状态变化，并与 LVR 关注的内部状态是否留存任务必要视觉细节、监督信息坍缩形成类比；但对象是外部字幕而非 latent 推理状态，需较多核查。
